pastry-chef.intro: Learn pastry from the ground up — baking fundamentals, decoration, food safety, and the business side of running a bakery. From home kitchen to commercial operation.

skillDomains.name: Baking Fundamentals
skillDomains.description: The science and technique of turning flour, sugar, and butter into pastry.

skills.name: Ingredients
skills.description: Know what each ingredient does and why it matters.

modules.title: The six core ingredients
modules.content:
1. Flour — structure. Different proteins for different pastries.
  2. Sugar — sweetness, browning, texture.
  3. Butter or fat — flavour, flakiness, tenderness.
  4. Eggs — structure, richness, moisture.
  5. Liquid — milk, water, cream. Hydration and richness.
  6. Leavening — baking powder, soda, yeast. Makes things rise.

Every pastry is a combination of these. Understand each one and you can improvise. Memorise recipes and you'll be stuck.

steps.q: Your cake is too dry. What likely happened?
steps.f: Dryness comes from too much flour or overbaking. Both are fixable next time.

steps.q: Your bread didn't rise. What's the most likely cause?
o: Dead yeast or water too hot
steps.f: Yeast dies above 60°C. Salt also kills it if in direct contact.

steps.q: Your pastry is tough instead of flaky. What happened?
steps.f: Gluten develops with handling. Overwork = tough. Handle minimally.

modules.title: Weigh, don't scoop
modules.content:
Baking is chemistry. Accuracy matters.

Cups and spoons vary by brand, by how you scoop, by humidity. A cup of flour can weigh anywhere from 120g to 160g depending on how it's scooped.

Rule

Weigh everything. A cheap digital scale costs very little and will improve your baking more than any recipe.

If you must use cups

Spoon flour into the cup, then level with a knife. Never scoop directly from the bag — it compacts the flour.

modules.title: The five dough families
modules.content:
1. Shortcrust

Flour + cold butter + water. Flaky. For pies and tarts.

2. Puff pastry

Layered with butter. Laminated through folding and rolling. For croissants and mille-feuille.

3. Choux

Cooked on the stove, then eggs beaten in. For éclairs and profiteroles.

4. Yeast dough

Risen with yeast. For bread and buns.

5. Sweet pastry

Higher sugar and eggs. For sweet tarts and desserts.

Master each one separately. They have nothing in common except flour.

steps.q: You're making a meat pie. Which dough?
steps.f: Shortcrust gives the flaky texture meat pies need.
Éclairs need choux — the only dough that puffs in the oven with a hollow centre.

steps.q: You're making a sweet fruit tart. Which dough?
steps.f: Sweet pastry is more sturdy and sweeter than shortcrust — ideal for fruit tarts.

skillDomains.name: Decoration
skillDomains.description: Turning pastry into something beautiful enough to sell.

modules.title: The three icings you'll use most
modules.content:
Buttercream

Butter, icing sugar, flavouring. Creamy, pipeable, holds shape. Best for piping and decorating.

Royal icing

Icing sugar + egg white or meringue powder. Dries hard. Used for cookies and fine decoration.

Ganache

Chocolate + cream. Rich and smooth. Poured over cakes or whipped for filling.

Choose the icing for the job. Buttercream on a cookie slides off. Royal icing on a cake cracks.

steps.q: You're decorating sugar cookies with fine details. Which icing?
steps.f: Royal icing dries hard and holds fine detail.

steps.q: You're piping rosettes on a wedding cake. Which icing?
steps.f: Buttercream holds shape beautifully and tastes good.

steps.q: You're glazing a chocolate cake for a glossy finish. Which?
steps.f: Ganache poured warm gives a professional mirror-gloss finish.

skillDomains.name: Food Safety
skillDomains.description: Protect your customers and your business.

modules.title: The five rules of kitchen hygiene
modules.content:
1. Clean hands — wash for 20 seconds before handling food, after using the toilet, after touching your face or phone
  2. Clean surfaces — sanitise work surfaces before and after every session
  3. Separate raw and cooked — different boards, different knives, different storage areas
  4. Temperature control — hot food above 60°C, cold food below 5°C
  5. Cover and label — everything gets a date and a name

Food-borne illness destroys a bakery's reputation overnight. A single case can end a business.

steps.q: You've just handled raw eggs. What do you do before touching anything else?
o: Wash hands for 20 seconds with soap
steps.f: Raw eggs carry salmonella. Wash immediately.

steps.q: A cake has been sitting out at room temperature for 6 hours. What do you do?
o: Check ingredients; if it contains cream or custard, discard it
steps.f: Cream and custard are highly perishable. Never sell dairy-based pastries left at room temperature.

steps.q: Your hands have a small cut. What do you do before working?
o: Cover with a waterproof bandage and wear gloves
steps.f: Cuts can harbour bacteria. Waterproof plaster plus gloves.

skillDomains.name: Costing
skillDomains.description: Price your work so the business survives.

skills.name: Ingredient Costing
skills.description: Know what every pastry actually costs to make.

modules.title: The cost per unit
modules.content:
You can't price a cake until you know what it costs to make.

Steps

  1. List every ingredient in the recipe
  2. Divide the package cost by the package size to get cost per gram
  3. Multiply by the amount used
  4. Add up all ingredients
  5. Add labour, overhead, and margin

Example

Flour costs 500 Le per kg = 0.5 Le per gram. Recipe uses 250g = 125 Le for flour.

steps.q: Butter costs 8,000 Le per 500g block. Recipe uses 200g. Cost?
Total ingredient cost is 5,000 Le. You want 40% margin. Price?
steps.f: 5,000 × 1.40 = 7,000 Le. But this doesn't include labour — always add labour too.

skillDomains.name: Business
skillDomains.description: Turn pastry skill into a sustainable business.

skills.name: Finding Customers
skills.description: Build a customer base that returns and refers.

modules.title: Where pastry customers come from
modules.content:
1. Word of mouth — the strongest channel in West Africa. One happy wedding client brings ten more.
  2. WhatsApp Business — post photos, take orders, build a catalogue
  3. Instagram — visual platform, perfect for pastries
  4. Event referrals — weddings, birthdays, corporate events
  5. Corporate orders — offices ordering for meetings

The best marketing is a beautiful product and a customer who talks about it.

modules.title: Price a wedding cake
modules.prompt: A bride wants a 3-tier wedding cake serving 100 guests. Ingredients cost 45,000 Le. You'll spend 8 hours on it. Your hourly rate is 3,000 Le. Overhead is 5,000 Le. You want a 40% margin. What's your price and how do you present it?
modules.context: Wedding cakes are priced differently from everyday cakes. The client is emotional and time-constrained. Clear, professional quotes win.
